en.title: Minimum Set with at Least Two Integers in Every Interval
en.description:
Given closed integer intervals, find the smallest set of integers such that every interval contains at least two distinct integers from the set. The original text allows single-point intervals but does not define the output when there is no solution; this site's protocol specifies outputting −1 in that case, without removing any originally valid input range.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of first last. 1≤n≤100000, 0≤first≤last≤10⁹.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3; -1; 2. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Process intervals by right endpoint in ascending order, and by left endpoint in descending order for equal right endpoints, keeping the two largest numbers in the chosen set; when an interval is not covered enough, pick numbers as close to its right endpoint as possible.
